Apple silicon unified memory: The M1/M2/M3/M4 chips have a unified memory architecture (UMA) where the CPU, GPU, and other accelerators share a single pool of memory. This is different from traditional PCs where the CPU has system RAM and the GPU has separate VRAM.

Key facts:
- Unified memory means CPU, GPU, Neural Engine all access the same physical memory
- No separate VRAM, no data copying between CPU RAM and GPU VRAM
- Memory is shared, so the whole pool can be used for whatever needs it
- Bandwidth: M-series chips have high memory bandwidth (e.g., M2 Ultra ~800 GB/s, M4 Max ~546 GB/s)
- The amount of unified memory ranges from 8GB to 192GB+ across models
- LLMs benefit because you can load the entire model into unified memory and the GPU/Neural Engine can access it directly
